$ flow tasks http
http
  Perform an HTTP request and return the response.

  inputs   url*                      string, a URI
           method                    string, 3 to 6 characters, matching
                                     ^(?i)(GET|POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE)$
           headers                   map[string, string], may hold a secret
                                     reference
           body                      string
           bearer                    any, may hold a secret reference
           credential                string, 1 to 128 characters, matching
                                     ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$, names a deployment
                                     credential target
           outputs                   map[string, any], evaluated by the task
           query                     map[string, any]
           json                      any, may hold a secret reference
           form                      map[string, any], may hold a secret
                                     reference
           expect                    any, must be written as an expression,
                                     evaluated by the task
           parse_json                bool
           retry_on_unknown_outcome  bool
  outputs  status_code               int, 100 to 599
           headers                   map[string, string]
           body                      string
           json                      any

* marks an input the task cannot run without.

Evaluated by the task, not by the engine: expect, outputs
The engine resolves an expression before it schedules the step, which is why an
ordinary input cannot name something that does not exist yet. These the task
evaluates itself, in its own scope, after it has run far enough to have one: it
is how `http`'s `outputs` may name `status_code`.

A step that uses it:
  edition: v2026.2
  name: example
  steps:
    - id: http
      http:
        url: https://example.com/
$
